response.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS a FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), b1 AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) AS v FROM orderexecutions), s1 AS (SELECT per.a AS a FROM per, b1 WHERE per.a > b1.v), b2 AS (SELECT AVG(a) AS v FROM s1), s2 AS (SELECT s1.a AS a FROM s1, b2 WHERE s1.a > b2.v) SELECT AVG(a) AS avg_of_remaining_averages, AVG(a - (SELECT v FROM b1)) AS avg_excess_over_first_benchmark, AVG(a - (SELECT v FROM b2)) AS avg_excess_over_second_benchmark FROM s2

assumptions.assumption: Executions with NULL ordersmark are grouped together as one order (SQLite GROUP BY puts NULLs in one group); orders whose remaincount values are all NULL have a NULL average and drop out of the comparisons.
The first benchmark is AVG(remaincount) over all execution rows with non-null remaincount, not the mean of per-order averages. Comparisons are strict (>).
